value.first: For a 2-year-old, I'd use the chair method. It's the trial-tested gentle one: you stay in the room while she falls asleep, in a chair beside her bed, calm and quiet, no rocking or feeding. Pick a start night with no travel or illness coming. Do the same 20-30 minute routine every night: bath, book, bed, bedtime between 6:30 and 8:00. First, move her to her own room and bed with you in the chair.
value.second: Nights 1-3: chair right beside her bed, minimal touch, a short phrase like 'I love you - it's sleep time'. Then move the chair roughly every 3 nights: mid-room, by the door, in the hallway where she can see you, then gone. If she gets up, walk her back calmly every time, no lights, no chat. Expect protest, and expect night 2 or 3 to be worse than night 1. That's the old pattern breaking, not the method failing. All told it runs about 2-3 weeks.
value.third: Treat night wakings exactly like bedtime: back to bed, chair where you are that week. Never lock or hold her door shut. It's working when she falls asleep faster and stays in her bed more nights than not. Most families see real change within a couple of weeks if both parents stick to it. If she snores, gasps or pauses in her breathing at night, mention it to her doctor. I'll check in Friday. Dr. Kurt Bjorkman, a pediatrician, has a good video if you want to watch it done.
